summary: On node1, cron scheduling is now restricted to root and opsadmin via /etc/cron.allow (with /etc/cron.deny removed so cron.allow is authoritative). Created the opsadmin user, verified root and opsadmin can install/list crontabs while a test unprivileged user is rejected by crontab with "not allowed to use this program". Performed the mandatory single-node restart: captured pre-restart boot_id (83a0a80f...), issued a non-blocking systemctl reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed a new boot_id (df4b7e15...) and fresh uptime, then re-verified crond is active and the cron.allow restriction (root/opsadmin allowed, unlisted user denied) still holds post-restart.
actions_performed: Inspected baseline: OS (CentOS Stream 10), crond active, no /etc/cron.allow, empty /etc/cron.deny, opsadmin user absent
Wrote /etc/cron.allow containing root and opsadmin (root:root, 644 perms), removed /etc/cron.deny, restarted crond
Verified root and opsadmin can install/list/remove crontabs
Created a throwaway unprivileged test user and confirmed crontab access is denied ('not allowed to use this program'), then cleaned it up
Captured pre-restart boot_id and crond/cron.allow health baseline
Issued non-blocking systemctl reboot on node1; acknowledgement returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until reachable again; confirmed changed boot_id and fresh uptime, proving an actual restart
Re-verified crond active, cron.allow contents persisted, and functional allow/deny behavior (root/opsadmin allowed, new unlisted test user denied) post-restart; cleaned up second test user

evidence.requirement: Only root and opsadmin can schedule cron jobs (configuration)
evidence.summary: Baseline showed no /etc/cron.allow; opsadmin created and /etc/cron.allow written with root and opsadmin, cron.deny removed, crond restarted active.

evidence.requirement: Functional proof: root and opsadmin can schedule; other users cannot
evidence.summary: root and opsadmin successfully installed/listed crontabs; a test unprivileged user was denied with 'not allowed to use this program (crontab)', then removed.
Captured boot_id 83a0a80f-773c-4f3e-9137-1e7aa887b07a, crond active, cron.allow contents (root, opsadmin), cron.deny absent.
systemctl reboot issued via backgrounded nohup; command acknowledged and connection subsequently dropped (stream closed), confirming reboot proceeded.

evidence.requirement: Proof of changed boot identity after restart
evidence.summary: Node unreachable during reboot (timeout, connection reset), then reachable again with new boot_id df4b7e15-ff02-42de-a66b-18b9a459b1d9 and fresh uptime, differing from the pre-restart boot_id.

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of cron service, config, and access control
evidence.summary: crond active post-restart, /etc/cron.allow persisted with root/opsadmin, cron.deny still absent, root and opsadmin successfully scheduled/removed crontabs, and a newly created unlisted test user was denied crontab access, matching pre-restart behavior.
